title: Why the denominators do not add
subject: Mathematical reasoning
knowledgePoints: Fractions can be added when they describe equal-sized parts of the same whole.
A common denominator renames the parts without changing the quantities.
coldOpen: Two slices of the same pizza, cut differently, sitting side by side.

questions.prompt: Mia eats 1/3 of a pizza and Noah eats 1/4 of the same pizza. What fraction did they eat altogether?
questions.misconception: Adding numerators and denominators separately gives 2/7, but that changes the size of the parts.
questions.temptingBecause: Adding top to top and bottom to bottom looks like ordinary addition.

examBridge.prompt: Ella walks 1/2 km to the shop and 1/5 km to the park. How far does she walk in total?

distractorReasons.B: Uses a common denominator but forgets to rename the numerators.
distractorReasons.E: Finds the difference between the distances rather than their sum.

practice.prompt: A jug is filled with 1/2 litre and then another 1/6 litre. How much water is in the jug?
